svg.title: A prospective paired Knee training experiment
svg.desc: Two ConvNeXtTiny arms share a fresh ImageNet initialization, report-group split, view sampler, augmentation, optimizer, and twenty-epoch exposure. Only ordinary versus explicit report-addressed BCE differs. Both fits and held prediction arrays must be sealed before held numerical targets are read. No training has run; physical weights and image arrays are missing.
svg.text: Does explicit report-addressed supervision help?
Original paired ConvNeXtTiny protocol • prospective and untrained • no official score claim
Execution is closed until the exact physical assets are supplied.
Pinned ImageNet-22K → ImageNet-1K weight file and all 4,345 owned twelve-view image arrays are absent locally.
Frozen report-group split
Fit: 3,479 studies / 3,275 groups
Held: 866 studies / 815 groups
Fold 4 held • group overlap 0 • Gold 58 excluded
One shared fresh initialization and training schedule
ConvNeXtTiny 768 → 512 • six-slot attention MIL • twelve fixed views
Same seed, epoch order, flips, AdamW, FP32, effective batch 4
Only the loss weights differ. Both arms load the same sealed initial tensor state.
Arm A · ordinary soft BCE
Every finding receives weight 1.
Exactly 20 epochs; final checkpoint only.
Unmentioned findings retain the supplied soft probabilities.
Arm B · addressed soft BCE
Use explicit source m_finding masks.
Exactly 20 epochs; final checkpoint only.
Each finding is normalized by its effective-batch support.
Both fits sealed → both held prediction arrays sealed → numerical held labels
Paired AUC against addressed report targets; 5,000 report-group bootstrap draws; all twelve findings retained.
Same-source, reused-fold diagnostic. Passing the prospective screen permits further independent validation only.
CPU loss-gradient and sampler contracts passed. Actual pretrained loading, image authentication, training and score quality remain untested.
